country.comment: Rural Cambodia, specifically 30 villages across four districts in Kampong Chhnang province in the Tonle Sap Lake region.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title & Abstract; PDF p. 4, Sampling frame and sample size; PDF p. 7, Sustainability and scalability of the mechanism

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative headline estimates from household logistic regressions (village-clustered SEs) and village-level OLS regressions across 30 villages (2,821 unique household sales presentations; 437 total latrine orders: 326 treatment, 111 control). Note that latrine sales reflect orders rather than verified installations.
effect_estimate.value: Offering a 50% targeted latrine subsidy increased the predicted probability of latrine purchase among eligible households by 31.3 percentage points (marginal probability = 0.313, p = 0.00; reported in text as 31 percentage points) relative to ineligible control households; household sales closing rates in treatment villages were 38% among subsidy-offered eligible households vs. 6% among ineligible households (p = 0.00), compared with 8% vs. 6% in control villages (p = 0.32), and overall sales conversion was 22% in treatment areas vs. 7% in control areas (p = 0.00). At the village level, offering subsidies increased overall village sales closing rates by 23 percentage points (p = 0.00) and increased latrine purchase rates among subsidy-qualifying households by 32 percentage points (32%, p = 0.00), including +37 percentage points among PPI-qualifying households (p = 0.00) and +26 percentage points (26%, p = 0.03) among IDPoor households. Direct household climate vulnerability increased purchase probability under a subsidy offer by an additional 10 percentage points (p = 0.00). No significant market distortion was found among ineligible households (only 3 of 2,352 non-purchasing households reported waiting on a subsidy), and programmatic cost per latrine sold was USD 224.22 in treatment areas vs. USD 602.07 in control areas (overall USD 320.20).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract & Highlights; PDF pp. 6–8, Results & Table 1

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cluster-randomized controlled trial (appraised with RoB 2 cluster-RCT variant) experimentally randomizing the targeted subsidy eligibility and price-discount mechanism across 30 villages and directly testing its causal effect on household latrine purchase uptake, though with implementation caveats (unblinded sales agents/village leaders yielding slightly higher IDPoor share in treatment villages [51–52% vs. 45% overall eligibility, p = 0.00], and outcomes measured as orders rather than verified installations).
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 2, Introduction; PDF pp. 4–6, Methods & Results; PDF pp. 8–9, Limitations

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines a two-layer targeted sanitation subsidy eligibility mechanism combining government IDPoor registration, a 10-question Poverty Probability Index (PPI) proxy means test, commune Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI) scores, and household climate-shock criteria (differentiated PPI thresholds accommodating poverty and climate hardship), paired with a 50% upfront latrine price discount (~USD 70 Easy Latrine / ~USD 140 Sky Latrine; average subsidy USD 44.84), door-to-door outreach/screening by trained agents with village authority assistance, and 10% M&E verification spot checks.
